Spatial Phylogenetic or Functional Redundancy Accumulation

Source: R/redundancy.R
spaccRedundancy.Rd

Track how much of the taxonomic diversity added along the spatial accumulation is new phylogenetic or functional diversity, as the ratio of the taxonomic Hill number to the phylogenetic or functional Hill number of the accumulated community.

Usage

spaccRedundancy(
  x,
  coords,
  tree = NULL,
  traits = NULL,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  n_seeds = 50L,
  method = c("knn", "nn_walk"),
  distance = c("euclidean", "haversine"),
  dist_method = c("euclidean", "gower"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  progress = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  focal_points = NULL,
  focal_domain = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A site-by-species matrix (abundance or presence/absence).

coords

A data.frame with columns x and y, or a spacc_dist object.

tree

A phylogenetic tree of class phylo with branch lengths. Supply either tree or traits.

traits

A species-by-traits matrix or data.frame, row names matching the columns of x.

q

Numeric vector. Orders of diversity. Default c(0, 1, 2).

n_seeds

Integer. Number of random starting points. Default 50.

method

Character. Accumulation method: "knn" or "nn_walk".

distance

Character. Site distance method: "euclidean" or "haversine".

dist_method

Character. Trait distance for traits: "euclidean" on standardised traits (default) or "gower".

normalize

Logical. Rescale trait distances to a maximum of 1. Default TRUE.

parallel

Logical. Use parallel processing? Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer. Number of cores.

progress

Logical. Show progress? Default TRUE.

seed

Integer. Random seed.

focal_points

Optional focal points for method = "knn". See spacc().

focal_domain

Optional polygonal focal domain. See spacc().

Value

An object of class spacc_redundancy containing:

curves

Named list (one per q) of n_seeds x n_sites matrices of the ratio taxonomic / phylogenetic or functional Hill number

taxonomic

The taxonomic Hill numbers, same layout

dimension

The phylogenetic or functional Hill numbers, same layout

type

"phylogenetic" or "functional"

q, coords, n_seeds, n_sites, n_species, method, orders

Parameters and the site orders used

Details

At each accumulation step the function computes, for every order q, the taxonomic Hill number \(^qD\) of the accumulated community and either its phylogenetic Hill number \(^qD(T)\) (Chao et al. 2010; effective number of equally abundant, equally distinct lineages, with \(T\) the abundance-weighted mean root-to-tip depth) or its similarity-sensitive functional Hill number \(^qD^Z\) (Leinster & Cobbold 2012; with \(Z = 1 - d\) from trait distances). The ratio $$R_q = {}^qD / {}^qD(T) \quad \textrm{or} \quad {}^qD / {}^qD^Z$$ is at least 1, equal to 1 when species are maximally distinct (a star tree, or every pair of species at the maximal trait distance), and grows as the species added are close relatives or functionally similar to those already present. A ratio rising along the curve says the area is adding species faster than lineages or trait combinations.

References

Chao, A., Chiu, C.-H. & Jost, L. (2010). Phylogenetic diversity measures based on Hill numbers. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 365, 3599-3609.

Leinster, T. & Cobbold, C.A. (2012). Measuring diversity: the importance of species similarity. Ecology, 93, 477-489.

Alberdi, A. & Gilbert, M.T.P. (2019). A guide to the application of Hill numbers to DNA-based diversity analyses. Molecular Ecology Resources, 19, 804-817. doi:10.1111/1755-0998.13014

See also

spaccHill(), spaccPhylo(), spaccFunc(), diversityProfile()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tree <- ape::rcoal(25)
  coords <- data.frame(x = runif(40), y = runif(40))
  species <- matrix(rpois(40 * 25, 1), nrow = 40,
                    dimnames = list(NULL, tree$tip.label))
  red <- spaccRedundancy(species, coords, tree = tree, n_seeds = 10)
  plot(red)
}
# }
